In the forests around Ab'Dendriel, {creature:White Deer} are hunted by wolves and poachers who want their antlers and hides, while the elves try to protect them. If players kill too many deer in a day, the next day {creature:Starving Wolf|Starving Wolves} appear instead of deer; capturing those wolves makes the deer come back. While there are deer you can loot {item:White Deer Antlers} and {item:White Deer Skin} and try to tame a White Deer as a mount ({wiki:Kingly Deer}).
There is a delicate balance between the lives of the White Deer of the Ab'Dendriel forest and those of the wolves.

Ask any {wiki:Guide NPCs|Guide NPC} about {key:overhunting} to find out what state the world change is in today (see the table in section 1).
If you want to tame a White Deer, do it before the deer are overhunted.
This world change alternates between two states: there are White Deer in the forest, or the deer have been overhunted and Starving Wolves appear. The change happens at server save.
Talk to a {wiki:Guide NPCs|Guide NPC} in any city and say {key:overhunting}. The answer tells you the current state:
There are White Deer in the forest.
There are still White Deer, but they are close to being overhunted.
There are still White Deer, but at the next server save Starving Wolves will appear.
There are Starving Wolves; the deer only return if the wolves are captured.

Take a boat to **Ab'Dendriel** (for example, with {npc:Captain Bluebear} in Thais: {key:hi}, {key:ab'dendriel}, {key:yes}). You arrive at the dock of {npc:Captain Seagull}, who also takes you back. Leave the city on foot: the forests where the deer roam start right around Ab'Dendriel.

The {creature:White Deer} roam the forests around Ab'Dendriel, from **Carlin** in the west to {wiki:Ulderek's Rock} (Orc Fortress) in the east. Kill them to loot {item:White Deer Antlers} and {item:White Deer Skin}.
Each dead deer reduces the population. If enough deer are killed in a day, they may not appear the next day (after server save) and are replaced by Starving Wolves.
Beware of the {creature:Enraged White Deer} and the {creature:Poacher|Poachers} and {creature:Elf Scout|Elf Scouts} in the area.

Sell the {item:White Deer Antlers} and the {item:White Deer Skin|White Deer Skins} to {npc:Cruleo}, who lives near {wiki:Ferngrims Gate} (**southeast** of Ab'Dendriel and east of Kazordoon). Walk there and back through the forest.
Use a {item:Golden Fir Cone} on a White Deer to try to tame it as the {wiki:Kingly Deer} mount. This is only possible while the deer are not over-hunted.
With the deer over-hunted, the wolves starve. Capturing them lets the deer population recover by the next day.

The {wiki:Femor Hills} lie between **Carlin**, **Ab'Dendriel** and **Kazordoon**. With Premium, the quickest way is the {wiki:Magic Carpet}: talk to a carpet pilot (Darashia, Edron, Farmine, Svargrond, Kazordoon or Issavi) and say {key:hi}, {key:femor hills} (or {key:hills}) and {key:yes}. You land on the carpet at the top of the Femor Hills, next to {npc:Uzon}. You can also go on foot: the hills are **east** of Carlin, **southwest** of Ab'Dendriel and **north** of Kazordoon.
The {creature:Starving Wolf|Starving Wolves} roam the **east** and **west** sides of the {wiki:Femor Hills}.
Lure the wolf into a trap

On the ground around the Femor Hills there are {item:Magic Wolf Trap|Magic Wolf Traps}. Lure a Starving Wolf onto a trap to capture it and get a {item:Captured Wolf}. The most useful traps are **east** and **southwest** of the Femor Hills {wiki:Magic Carpet}.

Hand the wolf over to Benevola
Take the {item:Captured Wolf} to {npc:Benevola}. Each captured wolf helps the deer population grow again by the next day.
You can also simply kill wolves, but that is 10 times less effective than capturing them.

To go back, get on the {wiki:Magic Carpet} at the top of the Femor Hills again and tell {npc:Uzon} {key:hi}, the destination (for example {key:kazordoon} or {key:edron}) and {key:yes}. Without Premium, walk to Carlin (west), Ab'Dendriel (northeast) or Kazordoon (south).
